newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy parliament commission rejects mini-budget. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Italy parliament commission rejects mini-budget. [CORRECTED 14:00 GMT]

text.p: The budget commission of the lower house of Italy's parliament voted on Friday against the government's proposed 1997 mini-budget, senior opposition politician Giuseppe Pisanu said.
He told reporters the vote was 25 (corrects from 26) against to 24 in favour.
The proposed mini-budget will now go to the full Chamber of Deputies for a vote but the result was a severe embarrassment for the centre-left government of Prime Minister Romano Prodi.

The supplementary budget aims to reduce the 1997 budget deficit by 15.5 trillion lire ($9 billion) in the hope of keeping Italy on track to meet the deficit-to-Gross Domestic Product target needed to join Europe's planned single currency.

Measures in the package to raise 1997 revenue by bringing forward tax payments due on companies' pools of severance payment funds have been severely criticised by businesses and the main centre-right opposition Freedom Alliance bloc.

Mauro Paissan, a senior member of the Greens party which is part of Prodi's centre-left coalition, said the result of the commission vote was essentially a challenge to the government to put the mini-budget to a confidence test in the full chamber.

"Basically, what the (government) majority and the opposition have done is to ask the government to call a confidence vote," he told reporters. Political sources said two government supporters were among those who opposed the package.
